papers.title: A Study of Renyi Entropy in pp Collisions by ALICE Data- A Comparison with UrQMD Simulation and AI-Assisted Modeling
papers.abstract: In the present investigation a systematic study of order dependence and energy dependence of Renyi entropy calculated from the ALICE experimental data of charged-particle multiplicity distributions in pp collisions at the centre-of-mass energies \root s= 2.76, 7 and 13 TeV within the pseudo-rapidity interval and transverse momentum range as selected by ALICE collaborationc has been carried out. ALICE collaboration compared the experimental multiplicity distribution of charged particles in pp collisions by PYTHIA 8.306 and EPOS-LHC model and hence Renyi entropy has also been evaluated from the corresponding PYTHIA 8.306 and EPOS-LHC model results reported by the ALICE Collaboration. An independent comparison has been carried out using UrQMD simulation generated for the same collision energies and kinematic acceptance by the author himself. In addition, an AI-assisted multiplicity distribution is considered as an auxiliary statistical reference for Renyi entropy estimation. In all the cases, the Renyi entropy exhibits a decreasing trend with increasing order q, indicating the presence of multifractality in pp collisions. The values of Renyi entropy for a particular order increases systematically with the increase of collision energy from \root s = 2.76TeV to 13 TeV, reflecting the increasing disorder and dynamical fluctuations of the particle-production process.

papers.title: Measurements of inclusive $J/\psi$ production in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
papers.abstract: Inclusive $J/\psi$ production at mid-rapidity ($|y| < 1.0$) in Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon-nucleon pair ($\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$) of 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV is measured with the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. The nuclear modification factor $R_{{\rm AA}}$ is used to quantify modifications of $J/\psi$ production relative to an interpolated $p$+$p$ reference. The measured $R_{{\rm AA}}$ shows a hint of a decreasing trend from peripheral to central collisions, reaching a value of approximately 0.5 in the 0-20% centrality class across all collision energies. Unlike similar measurements in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 200 GeV, where $J/\psi$ $R_{{\rm AA}}$ shows little dependence on transverse momentum ($p_{\rm {T}}$), the corresponding $R_{{\rm AA}}$ at the lower collision energies of 14.6-27 GeV shows a tendency to increase with $p_{\rm {T}}$. Additionally, the inclusive $J/\psi$ $R_{{\rm AA}}$, integrated over $J/\psi$ $p_{\rm {T}}$, in central collisions exhibits no significant variation within uncertainties over the energy range of 14.6 to 200 GeV. These results can be qualitatively described by transport models that incorporate hot and cold nuclear matter effects.

papers.title: Inclusive and diffractive D meson photoproduction in $pPb$ collisions at the LHC using Pythia8 framework
papers.abstract: We present a systematic analysis of inclusive and diffractive $D$-meson photoproduction in $ep$ and ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions within the Pythia8 framework. Predictions obtained with different proton and Pomeron PDFs are compared with H1 measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^*$ photoproduction at HERA. We also present predictions for the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction at the LHC. Our analysis indicates that the diffractive contribution exceeds 15\% at low $p_T$ and forward rapidities, suggesting that diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction could be accessible in future LHC runs. In addition, measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions can help constrain the proton and Pomeron PDFs.

papers.title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
papers.abstract: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^\pi=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.
